question: How much annual leave can I carry over into the next leave year?
answer: You can carry over a maximum of 240 annual leave hours from one leave year to the next[2].

question: I've been a federal employee for 5 years. How much annual leave do I earn each pay period?
answer: You earn 6 hours of annual leave each pay period. [1]

question: What is the most award leave I can receive in one fiscal year?
answer: You can receive up to 80 hours of award leave in a single fiscal year[1][2]

question: If I leave TTS, will my unused award leave be paid out?
answer: If you leave TTS, any unused award leave will not be paid out [2].

question: How much sick leave can I use per year for a family member's funeral?
answer: You may use up to 13 days (104 hours) of sick leave per year for a family member’s funeral, bereavement, or funeral‑planning purposes[1].

question: How much parental bereavement leave do I get if my child passes away?
answer: You are entitled to two weeks (80 hours) of parental bereavement leave when a child passes away[1].

question: How many days of military leave do I get each year as a National Guard member or Reservist?
answer: You receive 15 days of Military Leave each year for active duty, active‑duty training, and inactive‑duty training as a National Guard member or Reservist[1].

question: What disability rating do I need for disabled veteran leave, and how many hours can I get?
answer: A veteran must have a service‑connected disability rating of 30 percent or higher to be eligible for Disabled Veteran Leave, and the leave provides up to 104 hours of paid time off[1].

question: If I'm approved for administrative leave to vote on election day, what is the maximum amount of time I can take?
answer: If administrative leave is approved for voting on election day, the paid leave is limited to the time necessary to vote and may not exceed three work hours[1][2].

question: What is the maximum number of credit hours I can have accrued at one time?
answer: You can have up to 24 credit hours accrued at any given time[1].

question: When does regular comp time expire, and what happens to it if I leave GSA?
answer: Travel comp time expires one year (26 pay periods) after it is earned, and any unused travel comp time is forfeited when you reach the expiration date or leave GSA [1]. General compensatory (comp) time also expires one year (26 pay periods) after it is earned, but if you leave GSA that comp time is paid out rather than forfeited [3].

question: What happens to my unused travel comp time if I leave GSA?
answer: If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is forfeited [1].

question: What is the most advanced sick leave I can request?
answer: You can request up to 240 hours of advanced sick leave, and if you are a term employee you may request up to the total amount you will earn during the remainder of your term [1][3].

question: How long do I need to have worked for the federal government to be eligible for FMLA?
answer: You must have at least one year of federal service to be eligible for FMLA[2].

question: If I take all 12 weeks of paid parental leave, how much FMLA do I have left for the next 52 weeks?
answer: If you use the full 12 weeks of paid parental leave, you will have no FMLA remaining for the next 52 weeks – the 12 weeks of PPL consume all of the FMLA entitlement you have for that period. [1][2]

question: After paid parental leave, how long do I have to agree to return to work?
answer: You must sign an agreement stating that you will return to work for at least 12 weeks after your final day of paid parental leave[2].

question: How much bereavement leave can I use per year for a civilian family member, and how much funeral leave do I get for an immediate relative's combat-related death?
answer: You can use up to 13 days (104 hours) of sick leave per year for bereavement of a civilian family member, and you may receive 3 days (24 hours) of funeral leave to plan or attend services for an immediate relative who died in combat[1].

question: Above what dollar amount do I need a receipt for a travel expense?
answer: Receipts are required for any expense that exceeds $75 (and for local‑voucher expenses the threshold is $25)[1][2].

question: What percentage of the normal M&IE rate do I get on travel days?
answer: You receive 75 % of the normal Meals and Incidental Expenses rate on travel days[1].

question: How soon after returning from a trip should I submit my travel voucher?
answer: You may submit your travel voucher for reimbursement as soon as you return from your trip[4].

question: Can supervisors get reimbursed for professional liability insurance, and how much?
answer: Supervisors may be reimbursed for professional liability insurance for up to half of the cost, with a maximum reimbursement of $150 [1].

question: How far in advance do I need to contact the Travel and Events team for official international travel?
answer: You must reach out to the Travel and Events team at least 7 weeks before your official international travel [1].

question: What counts as a 'large team gathering' that needs the event request process instead of an approval email?
answer: A “large team gathering” is defined as any event where more than six employees are traveling for an internal management meeting (not day‑to‑day business) and/or the group’s estimated travel expenses exceed $10,000. Such events must go through the event‑request process rather than relying solely on an approval email. [1]
